source.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
source.authors: Fabian Gloeckle; Badr Youbi Idrissi; Baptiste Rozière; D. Lopez-Paz; Gabriel Synnaeve

record.tranche_reason: The study compares induction-task accuracy after different training objectives, using a behavioral test rather than identifying induction heads or measuring their formation directly.
record.gate_note: The induction results in Figures 7 and S14 bear on induction behavior and its dependence on training objective and data. The paper does not measure loss-by-token-index in-context learning, a training-loss bump, or induction-head composition. Other downstream coding, math, and language benchmark results are not rows because they do not measure the induction behavior or training-time transition named in the claim.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1 and Appendix J train 1M–1B models from scratch on a behavioral induction test, varying the loss (next-token vs 2-token) and the data. The outcome is whether induction capability forms, which bears on V5. The study does not analyse heads, circuits, loss-by-token-index or training dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Correction: the text says the books mix removes the multi-token advantage except for the two smallest sizes (1M, 3M). The authors interpret multi-token loss as aiding cross-position information transfer, which favours induction-head formation. They argue that once induction forms, the task becomes next-token-solvable and multi-token loss slightly hurts on it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a behavioral repeated-name induction benchmark and compares training losses; it does not identify or intervene on attention heads or replicate the original circuit analysis or training-phase measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The induction advantage varies with model size and dataset composition: it appears for small models on children stories and mostly disappears with the 9:1 books/children-stories mix.
record.problems: The induction measure is a behavioral proxy, not a head-level or circuit-level analysis. Figure values are not stated numerically in the text. The children-stories evaluation uses an epoch oracle selected with respect to the test metric; the authors note that some evaluation name tokens never occur in training and that a perfect score is unreachable. The higher-quality-data figure does not state exact values or training duration.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other benchmark results, including GSM8K and coding evaluations, do not measure the induction behavior or training-time phase transition specified by the claim.

untested.parts: All of it: no head identification, previous-token-head composition or circuit analysis; only behavioral second-token accuracy.
All of it: no training curves are shown. 'Forms significantly earlier' with the books mix is stated but 'not shown here'.
All of it: no loss-by-token-index measure and no attribution of in-context learning to induction heads.
Induction behaviour forms at every tested size under some setup, but only one architecture family is used, heads are not identified, and no other modalities are tested.
Whether in-context learning persists over training; head-level formation; exact timing of formation.

missing.what: Direct dataset comparison at fixed objective (n=1): induction accuracy on children stories (Fig 7, at most about 0.5) vs books mix (Fig S14, at least about 0.85). The caption also says induction 'forms significantly earlier in training', but this is not shown.
missing.locator: Figure 7 vs Figure S14; Appendix J caption

record.verdict_notes: Induction is measured only behaviorally, with an epoch oracle chosen on the test metric. Values are figure only, with no uncertainty reported. The record's V1 and V4 links are unsupported because the rows compare objectives and data, not mechanism or cross-family presence. Coding, math and summarization results are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The test measures induction behavior on repeated two-token names, not attention heads, previous-token-head composition, or causal implementation by heads.
Tests a model-size sweep and two runs per objective, but not multiple model families, other architectures, or modalities; it does not identify heads.
Tests training-objective and dataset effects on the induction benchmark, not whether in-context learning persists in general.

relationships.condition: Children-stories training, models of 30M nonembedding parameters and below
relationships.reason: 2-token loss gives much better induction accuracy than next-token loss, which yields 'practically no' induction at small sizes. Formation depends on the objective (F7-1M, F7-3M, F7-10M, F7-30M).
relationships.display_finding: Two-token loss substantially improved induction accuracy, whereas next-token loss produced practically no induction at these small sizes.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Children-stories training, models of 30M nonembedding parameters and below
source_check.reason: F7-1M, F7-3M, F7-10M and F7-30M show substantially better behavioral induction with 2-token prediction. The text describes next-token capability as negligible or substantially worse, rather than uniformly negligible.

relationships.condition: Children-stories training, models of 100M nonembedding parameters and above
relationships.reason: The objective no longer changes induction accuracy at these sizes, so dependence on the training objective holds only for small models (F7-100M, F7-300M, F7-1B).
relationships.display_finding: The training objective no longer changed induction accuracy at 100M nonembedding parameters and above.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Children-stories training, models of 100M nonembedding parameters and above
source_check.reason: F7-100M, F7-300M and F7-1B qualify the objective effect: the 2-token advantage disappears at these sizes. This concerns the objective advantage, not absence of induction.

relationships.reason: With the books mix, induction forms earlier and higher (accuracy about 0.85–1.0 vs at most about 0.5). The data alone then removes the objective advantage except at 1M and 3M (S14 rows). The data comparison itself is partly confounded by out-of-distribution evaluation tokens, as the authors note.
relationships.display_finding: Adding books advanced induction and raised accuracy to about 0.85–1.0 from at most about 0.5, eliminating the objective advantage except at 1M and 3M; out-of-distribution evaluation tokens partly confounded this comparison.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Section 4.1 and Appendix J report earlier and stronger behavioral induction with the books mix, with the objective advantage remaining only at 1M and 3M. The numeric ranges in the verdict reason are axis bounds, not stated measurements; evaluation-token coverage also changes.

relation.reason: Controlled objective and dataset comparisons directly test training dependence of behavioral induction capability, bearing on V5.

tranche.reason: The study tests induction behavior under a new training-objective setting, comparing next-token and multi-token prediction across model sizes and training datasets.

source_check.notes: Induction is measured behaviorally, without identifying heads or circuits. Figure-only accuracies remain unquantified; absent row states refer to the objective advantage. Children's-stories results use test-metric early stopping over up to 90 epochs.

statements.correction: Section 4.1: 2-token prediction substantially improves induction capability at ≤30M nonembedding parameters; next-token models show negligible or substantially worse capability. Books:children-stories ratio = 9:1. Appendix J: induction develops earlier and reaches higher accuracy; evaluation tokens cease to be out of distribution. Exact accuracies are figure only.
statements.problem: The accuracy ranges are figure-axis bounds, not numerical results stated in the text. Negligible induction under next-token training is also overstated across all sizes through 30M: the caption allows either negligible or substantially worse induction.
